source_text: Eadem regula ueritatis docet nos credere post patrem etiam in filium dei, Christum Iesum, dominum deum nostrum, sed dei filium; huius dei qui et unus et solus est, conditor scilicet rerum omnium, ut iam et superius expressum est. hunc enim Iesum Christum, iterum dicam huius dei filium, et in ueteri testamento legimus esse repromissum et in nouo testamento animaduertimus exhibitum, omnium sacramentorum umbras et figuras de praesentia corporatae ueritatis implentem. hunc enim Abrahae filium, hunc Dauid, non minus et uetera praedicta et euangelia testantur. ipsa Genesis, cum dicit: dabo et semini tuo; hunc quando luctatum ostendit hominem cum iacob; hunc, quando dicit: on deficiet princeps de Iuda, neque dux de Femoribus eius, donec ueniat is cui repromissum est, et ipse erit exspectatio gentium. hunc Moyses, cum dicit: prouide alium quem mittas; hunc idem, quando testatur, prophetam uobis, dicendo, suscitabit deus ex fratribus uestris: eum quasi me audite; hunc, quando dicit: videbitis uitam uestram pendentem nocte ac die, et non credetis ei. hunc Esaias: prodiet uirga de radice Iesse, et flos de radice etus ascendet; hunc eundem, quando dicit: ecce uirgo concipiet et pariet filium,; hunc, quando sanitates ab eo futuras collocat dicens: tunc aperientur oculi caecorum, et aures surdorum audient: tunc saliet claudus ut ceruus, et Diserta erit lingua mutorum; hunc, quando patientiae uirtutes expromit dicens: non audietur in plateis uox eius; harundinem quassatam non conteret, et linum fumigans non exstinguet; hunc, quando eius euangelia descripsit: e dzsponam uobis testamentum aeternum, sancta Daud fidelia; hunc, quando gentes in ipsum credituras prophetat: ecce posui eum in principium et praecipientem gentibus. gentes quae te non nouerunt inuocabunt te, et populi qui te nesciunt ad te confugient; hunc eundem, quando ad passionem eius exclamat dicens: sicut ouis ad occisionem ductus est, et sicut agnus coram tondente se sine uoce, sic non aperuit os suum in humilitate; hanc quando flagrorum eius ictus plagasque descripsit: liuore eius nos sanati sumus; aut humilitatem: et uidimus eum, et non erat ei species neque honor. homo in plaga et sciens ferre infirmitatem; aut quod populus non erat crediturus: tota die expandi manus meas ad populum non credentem; aut quod resurrecturus a mortuis: e erit in illa die radix Iesse, et qui surget imperare gentibus, in eum gentes sperabunt, et erit requies eius honor; aut cum tempus resurrectionis: quasi diluculo paratum inueniemus eum; aut quod sessurus ad dextram patris: dixit dominus domino meo: sede ad dexteram meam, donec ponam inimicos tuos scabellum pedum tuorum; aut cum possessor omnium collocatur: postula a me, et dabo tibi gentes hereditatem tuam, et possessionem tuam terminos terrae; aut quod iudex omnium ostenditur: deus iudicium tuum regi da, et iustitiam tuam filio regis. nec hoc in loco plura persequar, quae annuntiata de Christo omnibus haereticis sed et ipsis ueritatem tenentibus magis nota sunt.
thought_title: Belief in the Son of God
pass_a_gloss: The same rule of truth teaches us to believe in the Son of God, Christ Jesus, our Lord God, but the Son of God, after the Father. This God, who is one and only, is the creator of all things, as has already been expressed above and earlier. For we read in the Old Testament that this Jesus Christ, the Son of God, was promised, and we observe in the New Testament that He was exhibited, fulfilling the shadows and figures of all sacraments with the presence of embodied truth. Abraham and David, not to mention the ancient prophecies and the Gospels, also testify to this. The book of Genesis itself says: I will give to your seed; it shows this man wrestling with Jacob; it says: the prince will not fail from Judah, nor the leader from his thighs, until He comes to whom it has been promised, and He will be the expectation of the nations. Moses says: provide another whom you will send; the same Moses testifies, saying: God will raise up a prophet from your brothers: listen to Him as you would to me; and when he says: you will see your life hanging night and day, and you will not believe in Him. Isaiah says: a rod will come forth from the root of Jesse, and a flower will ascend from his root; the same Isaiah says: behold, a virgin will conceive and bear a son; and when he describes the healings that will come from Him, saying: then the eyes of the blind will be opened, and the ears of the deaf will hear; then the lame will leap like a deer, and the tongue of the mute will be clear; and when he describes His virtues of patience, saying: His voice will not be heard in the streets; He will not break a bruised reed, and He will not extinguish a smoldering flax; and when he describes His Gospel: behold, I will make with you an eternal covenant, the faithful holy things of David; and when he prophesies that the nations will believe in Him: behold, I have set Him as a witness to the nations, a leader and commander of the nations; the nations that do not know you will call upon you, and the peoples that do not know you will flee to you. The same Isaiah, when he exclaims about His passion, saying: He was led like a sheep to the slaughter, and like a lamb before its shearer, He did not open His mouth in humility; and when he describes the blows and wounds of His scourging: by His stripes we are healed; or His humility: and we saw Him, and He had no form or beauty, a man in suffering, and knowing how to bear infirmity; or that the people would not believe in Him: all day I stretch out my hands to a people that does not believe; or that He will rise from the dead: He will be the root of Jesse, and He who rises to rule the nations, in Him the nations will hope, and His rest will be honor; or when the time of His resurrection: we will find Him ready like the dawn; or that He will sit at the right hand of the Father: the Lord said to my Lord: sit at my right hand, until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet; or when He is established as the possessor of all things: ask me, and I will give you the nations as your inheritance, and the ends of the earth as your possession; or that He is shown to be the judge of all: God, give your judgment to the king, and your justice to the son of the king. I will not pursue more things in this place, which have been announced about Christ, and are more well-known to all heretics, but also to those who hold the truth.

choices.why: referring to the presence of embodied truth

pass_b_english: The same rule of truth teaches us to believe in the Son of God, Christ Jesus, our Lord God, but the Son of God, after the Father. This God, who is one and only, is the creator of all things, as has already been expressed above. For we read in the Old Testament that this Jesus Christ, the Son of God, was promised, and we observe in the New Testament that he was exhibited, fulfilling the shadows and figures of all sacraments with the presence of embodied truth. Abraham and David, not to mention the ancient prophecies and the Gospels, also testify to this. Genesis itself says: "I will give to your seed" (Genesis); it shows this man wrestling with Jacob; it says: "the scepter shall not depart from Judah, nor the ruler's staff from between his feet, until he comes to whom it has been promised, and he will be the expectation of the nations" (Genesis). Moses says: "provide another whom you will send"; the same Moses testifies, saying: "God will raise up a prophet from your brothers: listen to him as you would to me" (Deuteronomy 18:15); and when he says: "you will see your life hanging night and day, and you will not believe in him" (Deuteronomy 28:66). Isaiah says: "a rod will come forth from the root of Jesse, and a flower will ascend from his root" (Isaiah 11:1); the same Isaiah says: "behold, a virgin will conceive and bear a son" (Isaiah 7:14); and when he describes the healings that will come from him, saying: "then the eyes of the blind will be opened, and the ears of the deaf will hear; then the lame will leap like a deer, and the tongue of the mute will be clear" (Isaiah 35:5-6); and when he describes his virtues of patience, saying: "his voice will not be heard in the streets; he will not break a bruised reed, and he will not extinguish a smoldering flax" (Isaiah 42:2-3); and when he describes his Gospel: "behold, I will make with you an eternal covenant, the faithful holy things of David" (Isaiah 55:3); and when he prophesies that the nations will believe in him: "behold, I have set him as a witness to the nations, a leader and commander of the nations; the nations that do not know you will call upon you, and the peoples that do not know you will flee to you" (Isaiah 55:4-5). The same Isaiah, when he exclaims about his passion, saying: "he was led like a sheep to the slaughter, and like a lamb before its shearer, he did not open his mouth in humility" (Isaiah 53:7); and when he describes the blows and wounds of his scourging: "by his stripes we are healed" (Isaiah 53:5); or his humility: "and we saw him, and he had no form or beauty, a man in suffering, and knowing how to bear infirmity" (Isaiah 53:2-3); or that the people would not believe in him: "all day I stretch out my hands to a people that does not believe" (Isaiah 65:2); or that he will rise from the dead: "he will be the root of Jesse, and he who rises to rule the nations, in him the nations will hope, and his rest will be honor" (Isaiah 11:10); or when the time of his resurrection: "we will find him ready like the dawn" (Isaiah 26:19); or that he will sit at the right hand of the Father: "the Lord said to my Lord: sit at my right hand, until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet" (Psalm 110:1); or when he is established as the possessor of all things: "ask me, and I will give you the nations as your inheritance, and the ends of the earth as your possession" (Psalm 2:8); or that he is shown to be the judge of all: "God, give your judgment to the king, and your justice to the son of the king" (Psalm 72:1). I will not pursue more things in this place, which have been announced about Christ, and are more well-known to all heretics, but also to those who hold the truth.
